info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package ingress is your front door: automatic TLS certificates and hostname routing to any backend, changed live.

get.summary: Returns every edge transform the caller's org has configured, ordered by id.
get.description:
Returns every edge transform the caller's org has configured,
ordered by id. A route names the ones it wants, in order.

post.summary: Creates or replaces one edge transform and hot-applies it.
post.description:
Creates or replaces one edge transform and hot-applies it. POST
mints an id when the body omits one; PUT takes the id from the URL, which wins
over any id in the body. type must be one of redirectScheme, stripPrefix,
addPrefix or headers, and stripPrefix/addPrefix each require their config key.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's edge transforms and hot-applies the change.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's edge transforms and hot-applies
the change. Routes still naming it stop being served (they compile as skipped)
until they name a transform that exists. Answers 204; an id this org does not
hold is 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the object to act on, from the path.

get.summary: Returns every routing rule the caller's org has configured, ordered by id.
get.description:
Returns every routing rule the caller's org has configured, ordered
by id. A route maps an exact Host (and optional path prefix) to a service.

post.summary: Creates or replaces one routing rule and hot-applies the new table — there is no config file and no restart.
post.description:
Creates or replaces one routing rule and hot-applies the new table —
there is no config file and no restart. POST mints an id when the body omits
one; PUT takes the id from the URL, which wins over any id in the body. A
route's host is a GLOBALLY unique DNS claim: a host another org's route already
holds is refused 409, so no tenant can hijack another's hostname.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's routing rules and hot-applies the shrunken table, freeing its host for another claim.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's routing rules and hot-applies the
shrunken table, freeing its host for another claim. Answers 204; an id this org
does not hold is 404.

get.summary: Returns every backend pool the caller's org has configured, ordered by id.
get.description:
Returns every backend pool the caller's org has configured,
ordered by id. A service is the weighted round-robin target a route dispatches
to.

post.summary: Creates or replaces one backend pool and hot-applies it.
post.description:
Creates or replaces one backend pool and hot-applies it. POST mints
an id when the body omits one; PUT takes the id from the URL, which wins over
any id in the body. A pool needs at least one backend and every backend URL
must be http(s)://host[:port].

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's backend pools and hot-applies the change.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's backend pools and hot-applies the
change. Routes still pointing at it stop being served (they compile as skipped)
until they name a pool that exists. Answers 204; an id this org does not hold
is 404.

get.summary: Status reports the ingress edge's live posture: the role this instance runs in (app or edge), whether its listeners are bound and on which addresses, the ACME posture (staging flag and certificate cache directory), how many hosts the compiled route table currently serves, and how many the ACME HostPolicy will issue a certificate for.
get.description:
Status reports the ingress edge's live posture: the role this instance runs in
(app or edge), whether its listeners are bound and on which addresses, the ACME
posture (staging flag and certificate cache directory), how many hosts the
compiled route table currently serves, and how many the ACME HostPolicy will
issue a certificate for.

get.summary: GetTLS returns the caller org's ACME intent together with the edge-wide TLS facts it lands in: which role this instance runs in, whether its listeners are bound, every host the ACME HostPolicy will issue a certificate for (the union across ALL orgs of TLS-marked routes and configured extraHosts, because one process holds one certificate cache), and the ACME directory and account email the process was started with.
get.description:
GetTLS returns the caller org's ACME intent together with the edge-wide TLS
facts it lands in: which role this instance runs in, whether its listeners are
bound, every host the ACME HostPolicy will issue a certificate for (the union
across ALL orgs of TLS-marked routes and configured extraHosts, because one
process holds one certificate cache), and the ACME directory and account email
the process was started with.

put.summary: PutTLS replaces the caller org's ACME intent and hot-applies what can be hot-applied.
put.description:
PutTLS replaces the caller org's ACME intent and hot-applies what can be
hot-applied. extraHosts are normalized and validated, then feed the ACME
HostPolicy on the reload this op performs, alongside the per-route tls flags.
acmeEmail and staging bind an ACME account for the lifetime of an edge process,
so they only take effect when the edge (re)starts — the returned note says so.

url.description: URL is the upstream server, http(s)://host[:port].

weight.description: Weight is this member's share of the round-robin; must be >= 0.

config.description:
Config is the transform's parameters: redirectScheme takes scheme (default
https) and permanent ("true" ⇒ 301, else 302); stripPrefix REQUIRES
prefixes (comma-separated, first match wins); addPrefix REQUIRES prefix;
headers is a header→value map set on the response.

id.description:
ID identifies the transform within the org: [A-Za-z0-9-_.], at most 128
chars. A create that omits it gets a generated one. Routes reference it by
this id.

type.description: Type is the transform: redirectScheme, stripPrefix, addPrefix or headers.

host.description:
Host is the exact hostname this route matches, lowercased with any trailing
dot stripped. It is a GLOBALLY unique claim — one route across the whole
edge may hold a host, so no tenant can hijack another's.

id.description:
ID identifies the route within the org: [A-Za-z0-9-_.], at most 128 chars.
A create that omits it gets a generated one.

middlewares.description:
Middlewares are the ids of the edge transforms to apply, in this order,
before the request reaches the service. At most 16.

pathPrefix.description:
PathPrefix narrows the match to requests under this path; it must start
with "/". Empty matches every path on the host.

priority.description:
Priority orders routes that share a host: higher wins, and equal priorities
fall back to the longer PathPrefix.

service.description:
Service is the id of the backend pool this route dispatches to. A route
naming a service that does not exist is skipped at compile, not served.

tls.description: TLS asks the edge to terminate TLS for Host with an ACME-managed certificate.

backends.description: Backends are the upstream servers to balance across: 1..32 of them.

id.description:
ID identifies the pool within the org: [A-Za-z0-9-_.], at most 128 chars.
A create that omits it gets a generated one. Routes reference it by this id.

passHostHeader.description:
PassHostHeader forwards the client's original Host header upstream instead
of rewriting it to the backend's.

acmeEmail.description:
ACMEEmail is the ACME account email. It binds an account for the lifetime
of an edge process, so it applies only when the edge (re)starts.

extraHosts.description:
ExtraHosts get certificates without owning a route — at most 256. They feed
the ACME HostPolicy and hot-apply on the next reload.

staging.description:
Staging issues from Let's Encrypt's staging directory (untrusted certs, high
rate limits). Like ACMEEmail it applies only when the edge (re)starts.

middlewares.description: Middlewares is the org's middlewares, ordered by id.

routes.description: Routes is the org's routes, ordered by id.

services.description: Services is the org's services, ordered by id.

acmeCacheDir.description: ACMECacheDir is where autocert persists accounts and certificates.

acmeStaging.description: ACMEStaging is true when certificates are issued from Let's Encrypt staging.

edgeEnabled.description: EdgeEnabled is true when the edge listeners are actually bound.

httpAddr.description: HTTPAddr is the address the ACME HTTP-01 + HTTP router listens on.

httpsAddr.description: HTTPSAddr is the address the SNI TLS terminator listens on.

liveHosts.description: LiveHosts is how many hosts the compiled table routes.

proxy.description: Proxy names the reverse-proxy implementation behind every route.

role.description: Role is "edge" when CLOUD_INGRESS_EDGE_ENABLED is set, else "app".

tlsHosts.description:
TLSHosts is how many hosts the ACME HostPolicy will issue a certificate
for. NOT a subset of LiveHosts: an extraHost owns no route, and a TLS route
naming a missing service is skipped while its host still wants a cert.

acmeDirectory.description:
ACMEDirectory is the ACME endpoint in use: the staging URL, or
"letsencrypt-production".

acmeEmail.description:
ACMEEmail is the account email the PROCESS was started with
(CLOUD_INGRESS_ACME_EMAIL), not the stored config's.

config.description: Config is the caller org's stored ACME intent.

edgeEnabled.description: EdgeEnabled is true when the edge listeners are actually bound.

managedHosts.description:
ManagedHosts is every host the ACME HostPolicy will issue a certificate for
— the union across ALL orgs of TLS-marked routes and configured extraHosts,
because one process holds one certificate cache.

note.description: Note states which fields hot-apply and which need an edge restart.

role.description: Role is "edge" when this instance binds the listeners, else "app".
